```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

```{r setup}
library(epicurves)
set.seed(1)
```

This vignette reproduces the simulation study and real-data application of
Article 1 (the SIRD-GA model) using only exported functions of this
package.

## Basic reproduction number and ODE mass balance

```{r r0}
sird_R0(lambda = 0.4, gamma = 0.15, alpha = 0.08)
out <- sird_ode_solve(times = 0:200, x0 = c(s = 0.999, i = 0.001, r = 0),
                       parms = list(lambda = 0.4, gamma = 0.15, alpha = 0.08))
range(out$s + out$i + out$r + out$d) # should be 1 throughout
```

## Simulation study

```{r sim}
N <- 20000
theta_true <- c(lambda = 0.4, gamma = 0.15, alpha = 0.08, s0 = 0.999, i0 = 0.001,
                 r0 = 0, p = 0.6, tau2 = 0.2)
sim <- sird_ga_simulate_obs(N, S0 = round(N * 0.999), I0 = round(N * 0.001), R0 = 0,
                             lambda = theta_true[["lambda"]], gamma = theta_true[["gamma"]],
                             alpha = theta_true[["alpha"]], p = theta_true[["p"]],
                             tau2 = theta_true[["tau2"]], Tmax = 100, Delta = 1)

fit <- sird_ga_fit(sim$y, N, Delta = 1,
                    start = list(lambda = 0.3, gamma = 0.1, alpha = 0.1, i0 = 0.002,
                                 p = 0.5, tau2 = 0.3),
                    n_sub = 6, hessian = FALSE, control = list(maxit = 1000, reltol = 1e-9))
round(fit$theta, 4)
sird_R0(fit$theta[["lambda"]], fit$theta[["gamma"]], fit$theta[["alpha"]])
```

Transmission rate and $R_0$ recover well; the recovery/mortality split
($\gamma$ vs. $\alpha$) is only partially identified from infection-only
data, consistent with the thesis's own appendix simulation (Scenarios 4-5),
where the sum $\gamma+\alpha$ is recovered far more precisely than either
rate individually.

## Real-data application: COVID-19 first wave, Paraíba, Brazil

```{r real-data}
data(paraiba_covid19)
data(paraiba_population)
y_raw <- paraiba_covid19$new_cases
y_smooth <- smooth_series(y_raw, 7)
```

Raw daily case counts carry pronounced day-of-week reporting artefacts
(lower weekend counts, Monday catch-up spikes) that materially affect the
Kalman-filter likelihood surface; `smooth_series()` applies a 7-day
centered moving average before estimation, as recommended for this
application.

```{r real-fit, eval = FALSE}
# Each start takes 2-5 minutes; not run automatically when building the
# vignette. See the summary table and discussion below for the results.
ms_real <- sird_ga_fit_multistart(
  y_smooth, paraiba_population, Delta = 1, r0_guess = 1.1,
  infectious_period_days = c(3, 4, 5, 7, 10),
  n_sub = 6, p_max = 0.98, control = list(maxit = 800, reltol = 1e-8)
)
ms_real$summary

fit_real <- ms_real$best

kf_real <- sird_ga_loglik(fit_real$theta, y_smooth, paraiba_population, Delta = 1,
                           n_sub = 6, keep_states = TRUE)
plot_sird_ga_fit(y_smooth, kf_real)
```

## A practical-identifiability finding: two basins, not one

Running `sird_ga_fit_multistart()` from five starting infectious periods
(3, 4, 5, 7 and 10 days) on the smoothed series produces:

| start (days) | loglik | $R_0$ | $\lambda$ | $\gamma$ | $\alpha$ | $\gamma+\alpha$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3  | 2947.3 | 1.027 | 0.736 | 0.541 | 0.175 | 0.716 |
| 4  | 2947.3 | 1.027 | 0.737 | 0.517 | 0.200 | 0.717 |
| 5  | 2947.3 | 1.027 | 0.736 | 0.683 | 0.033 | 0.716 |
| 7  | 2947.3 | 1.027 | 0.736 | 0.716 | 0.000 | 0.716 |
| 10 | 2924.0 | 1.034 | 0.229 | 0.093 | 0.128 | 0.221 |

Two distinct optima emerge, not a single flat ridge. Four of five starts
converge to a **fast-dynamics** basin: a stable optimum with
$R_0\approx1.03$ in which $\gamma$ and $\alpha$ individually vary freely
(0.00-0.70) while their sum stays pinned at $\gamma+\alpha\approx0.72$
(mean infectious period $\approx1.4$ days) — every split along this ridge
attains the *same* log-likelihood to one decimal place. The fifth start
converges to a **slow-dynamics** optimum, log-likelihood only $\approx$23
nats lower, with $\gamma+\alpha\approx0.22$ (mean infectious period
$\approx4.5$ days) — closely matching the published
$\lambda=0.26,\gamma+\alpha=0.25$ and consistent with established COVID-19
natural-history estimates, whereas the fast basin's 1.4-day infectious
period is not.

This is a textbook case for combining the raw likelihood with
epidemiological prior knowledge rather than reporting the unconstrained
MLE alone: the data mildly prefer the fast-dynamics basin, but its implied
infectious period is biologically implausible, while the slightly-worse
slow-dynamics basin is the epidemiologically defensible choice. Both the
$\gamma$/$\alpha$ ridge and the two-basin structure are consistent with,
and extend, the thesis's own appendix finding that $\gamma$ and $\alpha$
are estimated far less precisely than $\lambda$ or $R_0$ in simulation.
We recommend `sird_ga_fit_multistart()` as standard practice for any
SIR/SIRD Kalman-filter application to real incidence data, and report both
basins transparently in Article 1 rather than a single point estimate.
